title: American Politics: Landscape, Trends, and 2024 Shift
subtitle: Understanding the evolving political landscape, key players, and emerging trends shaping American democracy.

slides.title: American Politics in a Divided Era
Trend 1: The Rise of Populist Movements
slides.subtitle: Grassroots energy reshaping both major parties
bullets: 2016–2024: Trump-backed candidates dominating Republican primaries nationwide.
Example: 91 indictments across four jurisdictions; core base remains intensely loyal.
Democratic side: Progressive caucus pushing party left on healthcare, climate, and economics.
Note: Populist messaging appeals to voters feeling economically left behind by globalization.

slides.title: Trend 2: Partisan Polarization at Historic Peaks
bullets: 58% of Republicans and 55% of Democrats view the other party as 'threat' (2024 Pew).
Congressional gridlock: 118th Congress passed fewest bills since 1970s.
Social media algorithm amplification accelerating echo chambers and tribal identity.
Cross-party marriage and friendship rates declining; homogeneous social circles increasing.

slides.title: 2024 Election: Historic Dynamics Unfold
slides.subtitle: Biden exit, Harris surge, and Trump's legal battles
bullets: June 2024: Biden withdraws after poor debate performance; Harris emerges as nominee.
July–August 2024: Harris rallies Democrats; enthusiasm metrics surge above pre-debate levels.
September 2024: Trump convicted on 34 counts in New York; appeals ongoing.
November 2024: Trump wins presidency; Republicans control Senate; Democrats retain House.

slides.title: Trend 3: Voter Registration and Turnout Shifts
bullets: 2024: 68% voter turnout (highest since 1900); mail-in ballots exceed 35% of votes.
Gen Z voters breaking youth turnout records; climate and abortion key motivators.
Latino voter coalescence: 38% Republican (2024) vs. 31% (2020); gains in Arizona, Nevada.

slides.title: The Abortion Issue: Reshaping State Politics
slides.subtitle: Post-Dobbs decision creating powerful electoral force
bullets: June 2022: Supreme Court overturns Roe v. Wade; 21 states ban abortion immediately.
2024: 10 states vote to restore or protect abortion rights via ballot measures.
Example: Kansas (2022), Ohio (2023), Michigan (2024) all reject abortion restrictions.
Democratic messaging pivot: Abortion access now top-five issue for suburban women voters.

slides.title: Tech and Media's Political Influence Grows
bullets: Elon Musk's X algorithm amplifying conservative voices; blue-check removal causing advertiser exodus.
TikTok becoming dominant news source for Gen Z; algorithm favors anti-establishment content.
Fox News, MSNBC, CNN: primetime segments increasingly siloed by partisan narratives.
Misinformation spread: 64% of Americans cannot distinguish AI-generated from real images.

slides.title: Trend 4: Institutional Erosion and MAGA Influence
slides.subtitle: Republican Party transformation under Trump leadership
bullets: 2024: 83% of House Republicans voted against certifying elections (Jan 6 aftermath).
Trump loyalists controlling RNC, state parties, and election boards across Midwest, South.
Key insight: Traditional conservative institutions (NRO, Lincoln Project) marginalized; populist voices ascendant.
Capitol police still mobilizing for 2024 election security; January 6th trials ongoing.

slides.title: Democratic Party: Generational Reckoning
bullets: Biden's age (82) and fitness questions dominate first six months of 2024 cycle.
Harris's ascent signals younger, more diverse party leadership emerging post-Biden era.
Progressive wing (AOC, Bernie, Squad) pushing $15 minimum wage, student debt forgiveness.
Centrists (Newsom, Shapiro) advocating incremental reform; growing party tension on radical change.

slides.title: 2025 Outlook: Governance and Key Battlegrounds
bullets: Trump administration focus: border enforcement, tariffs, and conservative judicial appointments.
Congressional investigations: Republicans targeting DOJ, FBI, IRS for perceived political weaponization.
2026 midterms setting stage: control of Senate and House redistricting map-drawing power at stake.

slides.title: Challenges: Trust, Misinformation, and Democratic Resilience
bullets: Only 31% trust media institutions; 47% distrust government to protect election integrity.
Foreign interference: Russia, China, Iran running targeted ads; impact difficult to measure.
Note: US courts, military, and states have rejected election fraud claims since 2020.
Democratic institutions stress-tested but holding: Congress certified results, courts upheld rule of law.

slides.title: The Path Forward
bullets: Engage locally: voting, town halls, and community organizing remain core democratic power.
